qDomain.referenceChart: The original (R,Z,T), with T>=0, q=Q_ref*s>0 and 1/2<=s<=2.
qDomain.exactPrefixProof: The actual common b_n is monotone. For n>=N+1, b_n*q>=1; the original time cutoff and all its derivatives are exactly zero, including at the flat endpoint.
qDomain.bandFloorProof: q<2^(-(ell0+4)) implies -log2(q)>ell0+4. Every active |ell+log2(q)|<3/4 therefore has ell>=ell0.
qDomain.compatibleAtlas: For any two prefix orders valid at this same q, every extra coefficient is exactly zero together with all derivatives. The backgrounds, phases, original matrices, Volterra solutions, H and fixed positive a coincide by ODE uniqueness. The actual monotone b_n>=2^n makes these prefix domains cover every q>0.

proof: On the reference chart 1/2<=s<=2, the complete nearest-band candidates satisfy ell_ref-2<=ell_label<=ell_ref+2.
The declared q<2^(-(ell0+4)) and q>=Q_ref/2 imply ell_ref>ell0+3, so ell_ref-2>=8.
The original index f(ell)=((1+h)*ell*log2-2*log ell)/log Tg is increasing for ell>=8: log2>1/2 and2/ell<=1/4.
Thus i_label-i(ell_ref-2) is a nonnegative integer. The original certified four-band covering-difference bound gives i_label-i0<=4.

completeCommonTorusCoverProof.localFinitenessAndFlatJoins: For each fixed physical label, differentiate its complete local body first. In a reference chart the multiplier is ratio^(2A+a/2+b*D+c). Only then use the complete 81-candidate relabeling.

haarInvariance.rule: Every integer Jg^delta torus cover preserves normalized Haar integral: 14^delta inverse lifts times Jacobian14^(-delta) equals1.

completeCommonTorusCoverProof.fixedPhysicalRadialIntegration: The complete indexed operation reindexes at each radial integration argument. Labels active only elsewhere in the interval are therefore retained.
completeCommonTorusCoverProof.sourcePeriodicity: Jg^delta has integer entries. Every local compact rectangle has the original flat auxiliary joins, so the pullback is smooth and1-periodic in each common torus coordinate.

exactSmoothnessDerivation: Every retained local pulse is the original finite-interval linear Volterra solution with its smooth original coefficients. Differentiating the equation gives the retained finite variational systems.

The actual primary potential is multiplied by the original flat auxiliary cutoffs before its full curl. All local derivatives therefore have the same zero join across every compact rectangle boundary.
The original integer common-torus maps preserve smooth periodic joins. The complete locally finite81-box sum and all six full-curl products retain every sign and both torus Jacobian columns.

The pressure is the actual finite translated radial integral T0 of its full source with the original slow cutoff. Translation, integration, slow differentiation and products preserve this smooth1-periodicity.

The complete Etheta and Ez are finite differential expressions in those exact bodies. The FTC tail below is generated from their actual derivatives, not supplied numerical or theorem-reference bounds.

tails.lattice: All k in Z^2 with max(|k0|,|k1|)>K
proof: For the largest nonzero frequency component, r=m+4 integrations by parts give |Fhat(k)|<=C_r/((2*pi)^r*|k|max^r).
|1/(v_t.k)|<=(2+sqrt(2))*|k|max, and an output torus derivative of total order m contributes at most (2*pi)^m*|k|max^m.
Each max-norm shell n has 8n lattice points; its total is bounded by 8*(2+sqrt(2))*C_r/(2*pi)^5*n^-2.
The positive decreasing-series bound sum_(n=K+1)^infinity n^-2 <= integral_K^infinity x^-2 dx = 1/K retains every omitted mode.
